title: Correct final answer for l
description: Essential: The student's final expression for the water height l must be algebraically equivalent to l = (ρgH / (p₀ + ρgH)) * h.

title: Correct final answer for V
description: Essential: The student's final expression for the pumped air volume V must be algebraically equivalent to V = (ρg S H h) / p₀.

title: Applies Boyle's Law correctly
description: Important: The solution correctly applies Boyle's Law (pV constant) to relate the gas states in both parts of the problem.

title: Correct hydrostatic pressure relation
description: Important: The solution correctly states that the gas pressure inside the bell equals atmospheric pressure plus ρg times the depth of the air-water interface below the surface.

title: Identifies initial and final volumes
description: Important: The solution clearly identifies the initial (V₀ = hS) and final gas volumes (e.g., V₁ = (h-l)S) for the first part.

title: Considers pressure for water expulsion
description: Important: For part (2), the solution correctly identifies the required gas pressure as p₂ = p₀ + ρgH to expel all water.

title: Algebraic manipulation and solving
description: Optional: The solution shows clear, logical algebraic steps to solve the simultaneous equations derived from Boyle's Law and the pressure condition.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: The solution includes a check or statement that the units of the final answers (l and V) are correct (length and volume, respectively).

title: Incorrect pressure at gas interface
description: Pitfall: The solution incorrectly uses the total depth H (instead of H-l) for the gas pressure in part (1), leading to p₁ = p₀ + ρgH.

title: Sign or arithmetic error
description: Pitfall: The solution contains a fundamental sign error in the pressure equation or makes a critical arithmetic mistake in solving for l or V.
